A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MovingDroneCrowd dataset and video individual counting method. All pages, equations, tables and figures are readable, including v2's added supplementary Sections A–D; v1 ends after its references.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset statistics, evaluations on MovingDroneCrowd and UAVVIC, backbone and attention ablations, and qualitative predictions.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds an FMDC comparison, frame-interval sensitivity results and supplementary qualitative predictions.

M1.justification: The DCFA architecture, shared-density subtraction, decoders, four MAE losses and counting procedure are retained. SDNet names the existing method. The residual term added to Equation 3 matches the residual module already depicted in v1's Figure 5, rather than establishing a new architectural component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate individual counting on MovingDroneCrowd and UAVVIC. Dense and sparse crowds, static and moving cameras, and varied lighting are already represented in v1. The supplementary examples do not introduce another dataset, task or distinct evaluation environment.

E2.justification: v2 adds the density-based FMDC method to the MovingDroneCrowd comparison in Table 2. All previously evaluated comparators remain, and the UAVVIC comparator set in Table 3 is unchanged. This is a targeted addition of a particularly relevant baseline.

E3.justification: Supplementary Figure 11 adds an evaluation varying the test frame interval from 2 to 10. Existing benchmark splits and metrics remain unchanged. Appendix A's training interval range, test interval and resizing limits are newly disclosed settings, not evidence that the retained experiments changed.

E4.justification: v2 adds frame-interval sensitivity analysis and qualitative cases examining low-light dense/sparse scenes and a nearly static UAVVIC scene. The backbone, positional-encoding, DCFA-versus-SCFA and learning-strategy ablations in Table 4 remain unchanged; 'Subtraction' is renamed 'SDNet'.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars. The added interval analysis also presents point estimates without uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing numerical entries in Tables 2–4 are unchanged. v2 adds FMDC results, including MAE 120.31 and RMSE 183.57, interval-sensitivity results and qualitative predictions. Figure 3 also changes dataset-distribution bars: the training-set bin for 150–199 pedestrians moves from below 1% to above 1%, without an explanation.

T1.justification: Equation 3 adds the omitted residual term after cross-attention, correcting the formal recurrence to match the existing architecture diagram. No new theorems or proofs appear. Equation 1's shift from zero-based to one-based frame indexing is otherwise an equivalent reformulation.

C1.justification: v2 withdraws v1's repeated claim to the first density-map-based VIC method and reframes the methodological contribution around shared-density-map learning. It also drops explicit first-dataset assertions. These materially narrow the novelty claims, while retaining the dataset contribution and performance claims.

C2.justification: v2 attributes FMDC's weaker performance to difficulty predicting inflow/outflow masks. Supplementary Section D newly acknowledges shared-map errors, ambiguity from similar pedestrian appearances, and expensive cross-frame attention. These qualify the otherwise retained interpretations and applicability claims.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly documents frame intervals, resolution limits, learning rate, weight decay, scheduling, ImageNet initialization, PyTorch and A800 hardware. The abstract changes a promised code/data release to a reported release with an access link. These substantially improve reproducibility documentation, although v1's specific positional-encoding implementation reference is removed.

R1.justification: v2 introduces Wan et al.'s FMDC as the closest density-based predecessor and distinguishes shared-map estimation from flow-mask prediction, substantially revising the first-of-kind positioning. Smaller citation changes add Zhan et al.'s survey and remove the Twins, original ViT and Sreenu survey references.

P1.justification: The abstract and multi-paragraph introduction and related-work narrative are extensively rewritten and condensed around shared-density learning. SDNet terminology is introduced, explanations are edited throughout, and supplementary Sections A–D and acknowledgements are added. The main six-section outline remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 revises Figures 1–5, including clearer architecture labels and a redrawn distribution plot; reformats comparison tables with underlining and red improvement annotations; and relocates Figure 7. Four supplementary figures add dataset examples, prediction panels and an interval-sensitivity plot, substantially expanding the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps by recognizing and evaluating the closest density-based predecessor, narrowing the novelty claim, and supplying substantial training/testing documentation and reported code/data access. The sensitivity analysis and explicit limitations further strengthen assessment of the method. Although Figure 3's statistical revisions are unexplained and positional-encoding source detail is lost, the attribution and reproducibility gains provide a substantial overall improvement without relying on higher retained benchmark scores.
